h: Farnborough tips for happy little explorers
p: Because the sessions aren't on a strict timer, you can turn up at a time that suits your little one's routine rather than racing to beat the clock. For many families, that means arriving soon after breakfast when energy levels are highest, then heading home for lunch and a nap once everyone is happily worn out.

A few small things make a big difference. Dress the kids in comfy clothes they can climb and crawl in, and bring a spare set if there's any chance of messy or water play. A drink bottle for each child helps keep everyone going, and a snack in the bag can ward off the mid-morning wobble.

With a toddler and an older sibling, take turns choosing where to play next. Older kids often love helping younger ones in the role-play areas, and it can turn into the bit of the day they remember most.

Farnborough has a proud flying history, and that's a great thread to follow if your family enjoys a bit of extra adventure. The Farnborough Air Sciences Trust museum tells the story of British aviation research in the town, and the famous Farnborough International Airshow takes place every other year, filling the skies with aircraft.

For fresh air after a morning indoors, the Basingstoke Canal runs nearby, with towpath walks that are lovely for little legs and pushchairs. Neighbouring Aldershot has its own military heritage and green spaces too, so there's plenty to explore across this corner of north Hampshire.
